audit_items.proof_trace: The regular repay path (handle_repay:470) correctly calls enforce_post_borrow_repay_invariant after repay_debt, so the invariant holds there. However, liquidation_inner at line 774 calls unsafe_repay_debt_only directly without any subsequent enforce_post_borrow_repay_invariant call, meaning a close_factor-bounded partial liquidation (e.g., close_factor=50%, debt=150, min_borrow=100 → liquidator repays 75 → remaining=75 < min_borrow) can leave an obligation with sub-minimum debt, violating the property.
audit_items.attack_scenario: A borrower creates a position with debt slightly above 2×min_borrow_amount; a price drop triggers liquidation and a liquidator repays exactly close_factor×debt, leaving remaining debt between 0 and min_borrow_amount. The obligation is now stranded: handle_repay enforces the invariant and will revert on any partial repay, so the borrower is forced to fully close — but if the position remains undercollateralised the sub-minimum dust debt persists through further partial liquidations.
